actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.

dimensions.assessment: Affects Tibetan populations, the Central Tibetan Administration leadership, and U.S. Department of State diplomatic personnel.
dimensions.evidence: direct the Secretary of State to advocate for the inclusion and recognition of the Central Tibetan Administration

dimensions.assessment: Shifts U.S. foreign policy and diplomatic protocol to actively support and confer formal high-level recognition on the Central Tibetan Administration.
dimensions.evidence: ensure the Sikyong of the Central Tibetan Administration is extended appropriate diplomatic courtesies, including the provision of appropriate security details

dimensions.assessment: Involves standard diplomatic and security detail costs without specifying dedicated appropriations.
dimensions.evidence: provision of appropriate security details during visits to the United States

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a comprehensive statement of U.S. policy, UN voting instructions, diplomatic protocols, and mandatory annual reporting requirements.
dimensions.evidence: the President should direct the United States Permanent Representative to the United Nations to use the voice, vote, and influence of the United States... to advocate for the Central Tibetan Administration's observer status

dimensions.assessment: Mandates annual reporting for ten years alongside ongoing diplomatic policy guidelines.
dimensions.evidence: annually thereafter for ten years, the Secretary of State shall submit... a report

missing_information: Estimated financial costs for providing increased security details and diplomatic hosting.
importance_detail.rationale: Directs U.S. diplomatic efforts to advocate for the Central Tibetan Administration's international recognition and observer status at the UN, while mandating annual reporting.
